stem: A wound swab culture is ordered for a wound with clinical signs of infection. Which collection technique best supports an interpretable specimen?

options.A: Cleanse the wound, select about 1 cm² of viable wound-bed tissue, and rotate the swab with enough pressure to express wound fluid.
options.B: Cleanse the wound, then swab visible purulent drainage at the wound edge because drainage contains the highest concentration of organisms.
options.C: Cleanse the wound, then swab slough or eschar because devitalized tissue retains organisms longer than viable wound-bed tissue.
options.D: Collect exudate from the skin surrounding the wound before cleansing because surface organisms best represent the organisms causing infection.

rationale: Open RN Nursing Skills directs the nurse to cleanse and irrigate the wound to remove surface debris, identify about 1 cm² of viable wound tissue, and rotate the swab over that area with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid. The specimen should not be taken from pus, slough, eschar, necrotic tissue, or skin exudate. Therefore A is correct. B, C, and D preferentially sample material the source specifically directs the nurse to avoid and are more likely to yield a specimen that does not represent the clinically relevant wound bed.
educational_objective: For an indicated wound swab culture, cleanse the wound and obtain the specimen from viable wound-bed tissue using pressure sufficient to express wound fluid rather than sampling pus, devitalized tissue, or surrounding-skin exudate.
source_organization: Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN) / Chippewa Valley Technical College; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Nursing Skills [Internet], 2nd edition, Chapter 20: Wound Care
source_locator: Section 20.9 Checklist for Wound Culture, steps 9–20: irrigate/cleanse the wound to remove surface debris and contaminants; identify a 1-cm² area of viable wound tissue; do not sample pus, slough, eschar, or necrotic tissue; rotate the swab over the selected area for 5 seconds with sufficient pressure to express wound fluid; never collect exudate from the skin.
source_claim_supported: An indicated wound swab culture should be collected from cleansed viable wound-bed tissue using sufficient pressure to express wound fluid, while avoiding pus, devitalized material, and surrounding-skin exudate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p. 42: monitor results of diagnostic testing and intervene as needed; obtain specimens other than blood for diagnostic testing; use precautions to prevent injury and/or complications associated with a procedure or diagnosis.
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — wound culture specimen collection
correction_summary: Rebuilt all four options to remove the uniquely-long keyed answer and convert the distractors into realistic specimen-selection errors. The corrected item preserves the wound-culture technique construct with a direct NCBI checklist locator and a direct 2026 NCSBN specimen-collection activity statement.

audit_findings.stem: PASS — explicitly states that culture is clinically indicated and asks one specimen-collection technique question.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS — directly matches the source-supported viable-tissue and pressure-swab technique; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — purulent drainage is a plausible target but the cited checklist specifically directs the nurse not to sample pus.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — slough/eschar can contain organisms but are specifically excluded from the recommended culture site.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — surrounding-skin exudate is specifically excluded because it does not represent the cleansed viable wound bed.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — only A follows all material specimen-quality steps in the cited checklist.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — B, C, and D each select a specimen source explicitly excluded by the source.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — the keyed option is not the longest and all options are comparable in length and specificity.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Reduction of Risk Potential explicitly includes obtaining nonblood diagnostic specimens and monitoring diagnostic testing.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether purulent drainage or devitalized tissue might better reflect infection; the cited checklist directly excludes those materials and directs sampling of cleansed viable tissue with pressure, leaving A uniquely correct.
